boardSize.title: Board size
boardSize.help: How many tiles the board is built from. Everyone sees the same layout. On **Auto** the board is sized so roughly a third of it ends up mined.

bombCount.title: Bombs each
bombCount.help: How many bombs every player hides at the start. Nobody sees anybody else's. On **Auto** a smaller table hides more of them each.

lifeCount.title: Lives each
lifeCount.help: How many bombs a player can step on before they are out. On **Auto** a bigger table starts with fewer, since turns are shared out further.

stackedBombs.title: Stacked bombs
stackedBombs.help: Two players can hide a bomb on the same tile without knowing it. With this on, standing there costs a life for each of them.
stackedBombs.helpWarning: Turning this on makes a well-guessed tile far more punishing.

hideTime.title: Hiding time
hideTime.help: How long everyone gets to hide their bombs. Anything still unplaced when it runs out is hidden for you, at random.

default.title: Showdown
description: Board, bombs and lives scale to the table

minefield.title: Minefield
description: Stacked bombs cost a life apiece

suddenDeath.title: Sudden Death
description: One wrong tile and you are out

rules.title: Rules
description: Everyone hides the same number of bombs on one shared board. Nobody sees anybody else's, and you only see your own for a moment before play starts.
Players then take turns stepping on a tile. If a bomb was under it, whoever stood there loses a life. Every tile stepped on is out of the game either way.

memory.title: Memory
description: Your own bombs are live for you too, so remembering where you put them is half the game.
The other half is watching everybody else: where somebody hesitates, and where they refuse to go, is the best clue you will get about the tiles you cannot see.

winning.title: Winning
description: The last player with lives left wins.
If the board runs out of tiles first, whoever has the most lives left wins instead.

bots.title: Bots
description: Bots hide their bombs at random and step at random. The harder ones remember to walk around their own; the easiest ones forget where they put them, exactly like everybody else.
